How Many Types of Sequential Circuits Are There?

How many types of sequential circuits are there? There are two main types: synchronous sequential circuits and asynchronous sequential circuits. The split depends on how the memory elements change state. In a synchronous circuit all flip-flops change only at clock instants, while in an asynchronous circuit the state changes as soon as the inputs change.

ClassificationTypeKey featureExample
By timing (main)SynchronousState changes only with the clock signalSynchronous counters, shift registers
By timing (main)AsynchronousState changes directly with input changes, no common clockRipple counter, SR latch circuits
Synchronous subtypeLevel triggeredResponds while the clock is HIGH or LOWGated latches
Synchronous subtypeEdge triggeredResponds only at the rising or falling clock edgeD and JK flip-flop circuits
Asynchronous subtypeFundamental modeOnly one input changes at a time, circuit settles before the next changeHandshake and control logic
Asynchronous subtypePulse modeInputs are pulses that trigger state changesPulse driven counters
By output modelMoore machineOutput depends only on present stateTraffic light controller
By output modelMealy machineOutput depends on present state and inputsSequence detector

So the short exam answer is two types, synchronous and asynchronous. The other rows are subdivisions and design models that are built on top of these two.
